dial.summary: BTC Accumulation holds on Sep 10 with 5 of 8 indicators supportive — Global M2 expanding (~$103.4T July G4 composite), 2s10s steepening to +41bps on a 4-week basis, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.74T, BTC funding rates near zero (~0.008%), and stablecoin dominance in a sustained 30-day downtrend (11.04% confirmed Sep 10, $307B / $2.78T TOTAL); DXY has weakened further to 98.75 (4-month low, still neutral 97.5–100 band), BTC.D at 57.48% remains firm above the 55% alt-rotation threshold, with today's triple-event day (PPI 8:30 ET + ECB rate decision + Jobless Claims) and tomorrow's CPI (Sep 11) the last major data catalysts before FOMC Sep 16 (~60% hike probability).

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June 2026 global G4 M2 at $102,663.81B ($102.66T); July YoY growth rates at 4.67–4.81% per MacroMicro; broader global broad money supply (all central banks) reached a record $150T in June 2026 per Cointelegraph/SpendNode Sep 2 report — G4 aggregate of $103.4T is consistent with this (G4 ≈ 69% of global total); 4-week uptrend confirmed on July G4 composite vs June confirmed ($102.66T → ~$103.4T = +$0.7T, above flat threshold); August global 4-bank aggregate not yet published (expected mid-October); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); today's ECB Sep 10 rate decision and FOMC Sep 16 (~60% hike probability) are the next catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI (Sep 3) was 55.4% (beat 54.1% forecast), signaling continued services-sector expansion; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); reading of 54.6% corresponds to approximately 2.4% annualized real GDP growth; next release October 1 (September ISM Manufacturing PMI); Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey (Sep 17) will provide the next manufacturing-sector read before October ISM.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.75 (98.7484) on September 10, 2026 — down 0.05% from the previous session and sliding for the third straight session to its weakest level in four months; 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August 2026 to 98.75 on Sep 10 = −2.2% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 98.75 within the 97.5–100 neutral band, approaching but not yet at the supportive sub-97.5 threshold); dollar weakening driven by yen strength (BOJ hawkish expectations), carry-trade unwind, and reduced hike premium as market reprices post-NFP; today's ECB rate decision (8:15 AM ET) and PPI August (8:30 AM ET) are the key DXY directional triggers — an ECB hike + hot PPI could push DXY back above 100 (headwind threshold); CPI Sep 11 is the final major catalyst before FOMC Sep 16 (~60% hike odds).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.42% as of September 3, 2026 (most recent confirmed reading; FRED API egress-blocked this run, and Sep 9 H.15 value not independently sourced); nominal 10Y at 4.80% (Sep 8), 2Y at 4.39%, BEI ~2.30%, implied TIPS 2.42%–2.50%; 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% estimated Aug 9 → 2.42% Sep 3 = −1bp, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (flat trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition not fully triggered; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met); FOMC Sep 16 is the primary catalyst — a hike with hawkish dots would likely push real yields higher and re-activate the headwind status; CPI Sep 11 will update BEI and thus implied real yield.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 10, 2026: 2s10s spread at approximately +0.41% (+41bps); Sep 8 confirmed data: 10Y yield 4.80%, 2Y yield 4.39%, spread = 41bps; slight widening from +40bps on Sep 9 reflecting 10Y rising 1bp to 4.80% with 2Y unchanged at 4.39%; 4-week uptrend confirmed: ~+35bps (Aug 9 estimate) → +41bps (Sep 10) = +6bps net steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); next FOMC (Sep 16, ~60% hike odds) is the key risk: a hike would flatten the curve rapidly as the 2Y reprices faster than the 10Y, potentially reversing the steepening trend; the curve has steepened from deeply inverted (−50bps range in 2023–24) and has been solidly positive since H1 2026.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T (~$6.7T) for week ending September 2, 2026 (H.4.1 confirmed Sep 3); H.4.1 covering week ending Sep 10 is scheduled for release at 4:30 PM ET today (Sep 10) — not yet available as of this morning run; 4-week trend flat: Aug 5 estimate ~$6.70T → Sep 2 $6.74T = +$40B, within flat threshold; FRED API egress-blocked this run — value confirmed from govspending.org and Fed H.4.1 search data; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike; no aggressive QT signal); this evening's Sep 10 H.4.1 release will provide the first read on post-ECB / pre-FOMC (Sep 16) liquidity conditions.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.008% per 8h (Sep 9, 2026; CoinGlass direct fetch egress-blocked this run; value sourced from WebSearch cross-reference: 0.0078% cited for Sep 9 market context); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; BTC.D at ~57.48% (CoinGecko Sep 10 — implied from $1.6T BTC market cap / $2.78T TOTAL market cap); well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action with no leveraged long crowding); alt-rotation trigger not met (BTC.D 57.48% well above 55% threshold, though slightly lower than prior run's 57.65%).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $307B (Sep 10, 2026; CoinGecko confirmed); total crypto market cap ~$2.78T (CoinGecko Sep 10: +1.13% 24h); stablecoin dominance 11.04% on Sep 10, 2026 — down from 11.09% (Sep 9) reflecting slight total market cap expansion; BTC market cap $1.6T, BTC.D 57.48% (confirmed Sep 10); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 11.04% = sustained ~2–3pp decline reflecting capital deployment into risk assets over the past month; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does not apply: stablecoin dominance is declining while TOTAL expands to $2.78T); USD stablecoins (USDT + USDC) hold ~83% of the $307B stablecoin supply.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; markets pricing ~60% probability of a hike after August NFP beat (+162K vs +56K consensus, Sep 4); DXY at 98.75 — the CPI print is the key trigger for a directional break above 100 (headwind) or toward 97.5 (supportive); a hot CPI above 3.8% YoY would likely lock in a Sep 16 hike; a soft CPI below 3.3% would pull back hike expectations and support risk assets; July 2026 CPI was 3.6% YoY; core CPI ex-food and energy is the primary Fed focus.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released same day as CPI August; captures 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; elevated 1-year inflation expectations combined with hot CPI would strengthen the Fed's case for a Sep 16 hike; a drop in confidence alongside cooling CPI would temper hike odds and create a risk-asset supportive setup heading into FOMC; watch 5-year inflation expectations closely as a long-run anchoring signal for the Fed's reaction function.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET (two-day meeting Sep 15–16), press conference at 2:30 PM ET; includes updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) with dot plot; current target range 3.5%–3.75% (held at July 28–29 meeting); markets pricing ~60% probability of a 25bps hike following NFP beat (+162K, Sep 4); data inputs ahead: PPI Aug (Sep 10), CPI Aug (Sep 11); dot plot and forward guidance are the primary DXY, real yield, and risk-asset drivers through Q4 2026; a hike + aggressive 2027 dots would push DXY above 100 and compress risk assets; a hawkish hold (no hike, hike-biased language) is the middle scenario; a dovish hold preserving the cut pathway would be the most risk-on outcome and the key trigger for a BTC directional move.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET); advance read on consumer spending ahead of FOMC deliberations; strong August NFP (+162K) suggests continued consumer income growth; a strong retail sales print (above +0.3% MoM) alongside hot NFP confirms Q3 consumer strength and may reinforce hike probability; a weak print (below 0%) would introduce consumer softening even amid labor strength, potentially complicating the Fed's calculus.

upcoming.title: Bank of England Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee rate decision at 12:00 PM London time (7:00 AM ET) — one day after FOMC Sep 16; BOE currently holds at 3.75% (held at the July 30 meeting; MPC voted 6-3 to hold, with Pill, Greene, and Mann voting to hike to 4.00%); market-implied probability of hold at approximately 90%; UK CPI rose to 2.9% YoY in July, elevated by Middle East conflict energy price spillover; if ECB hiked Sep 10 and FOMC hiked Sep 16, a BOE hold with dovish language on Sep 17 would create significant transatlantic monetary policy divergence and GBP/EUR volatility; BOE outcome will influence global risk sentiment entering the back half of September.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as BOE decision; a leading indicator for national ISM Manufacturing (next release Oct 1); prior August reading showed moderate expansion; a strong Philly Fed print would reinforce the ISM-above-50 backdrop and reduce near-term recession risk; the index is one of the earliest September manufacturing reads and helps calibrate expectations for the ISM Sep 1 release.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 13, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 13, 2026 — first labor-market read post-FOMC Sep 16; any significant spike above 220K would amplify rate-path repricing following the FOMC decision; released on the same day as BOE rate decision and Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.
